transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samira, Jonah, Diego, Maya, Ethan, Priya, Oliver, Hannah

Summary (auto): Weekly ops coordination - billing incident follow-up, SOC2 scoping, KMS rotation planning, and chargeback discussion.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'll kick off, we got a couple of things on the docket — billing spike post-mortem, SOC two scoping, KMS rotation, and then the reserved capacity chargeback conversation.
[00:18] Maya: Yeah, thanks. I'll be brief on the billing side, we saw a 42% invoice delta for mid-December. Looks like some runaway batch jobs plus a landscape of ephemeral dev clusters.
[00:33] Ethan: Sorry to interject, the FP&A numbers I pulled tie most of that to the holiday embeddings job — that job re-routed to Dedicated accidentally, which bumped unit costs.
[00:48] Hannah: Right and a follow up, billing tags were inconsistent so we couldn't allocate easily. A few requests came in with "redwood-dev" vs "eng-playground" tags, so chargeback missed them.
[01:05] Jonah: (murmur) Tagging is the root cause a lot of times. On the infra side we have a default routing rule that will route to Dedicated when specific headers are present; seems the CI pipeline added that header. I'm going to file a PR for a safe default.
[01:23] Samira: Good. Action: Jonah will patch the pipeline header guard, Hannah will produce a revised tagging doc.
[01:33] [crosstalk] Priya: Also, for SOC 2, we need to be explicit about data retention for embeddings and any ephemeral compute logs — are we storing KV caches anywhere persistent?
[01:48] Diego: The KV cache lives in node-local memory for runtime; persistent only if a debug snapshot is triggered. There were a couple of debug snapshots captured during that run, which were not scrubbed.
[02:05] Priya: Ok that matters. We should add a policy to scrub or avoid snapshots in non-prod unless approved.
[02:15] Maya: For the billing post-mortem, I'll ping the team to list all jobs routed to Dedicated between Dec 15–Jan 5. That will help quantify chargeback.
[02:29] Samira: Perfect. Switching to SOC 2 status, Priya where are we on the scoping spreadsheet?
[02:36] Priya: I started a draft in /confluence/security/soc2-scoping but it's rough. Need inputs from Platform, Infra, and Finance. Specifically evidence owners for change control and key rotation.
[02:50] Diego: For keys, the KMS is split: customer-managed keys for Private deployments and Redwood-managed for hosted. For the internal scoping we need to show rotation cadence and HSM attestations where we use HSM.
[03:05] Oliver: Treasury has a compliance requirement to know where customer billing keys are stored for PCI adjacency — even if we aren't storing credit card numbers, the mapping matters for audits.
[03:18] Samira: Let's make that an action. Diego to draft a KMS/HSM rotation plan with windows where rotation occurs, and indicate which envs use HSM.
[03:28] Diego: Will do — I already have notes from last year's rotation but will formalize.
[03:33] [00:03:45] Hannah: On the chargeback model, Finance needs scenarios: flat allocation vs true usage with reserved discounts rolled in. There are also hybrid models where infra gets a base allocation and teams pay overages.
[03:55] Ethan: The reserved capacity product complicates things — commits reduce unit cost but create forecasting risk. We need a metric like committed utilization % to apportion cost.
[04:09] Samira: Can we simulate three scenarios and show 12-month impact? Hannah?
[04:15] Hannah: Yes, I'll draft three: flat, usage, hybrid. I'll include committed utilization and a threshold for automatic top-ups.
[04:26] Jonah: Quick technical detail — the runtime exposes token-level metrics but not per-tenant GPUs in the current console; I'll add a tag to the metrics pipeline so Finance can slice by team. That will help the chargeback modeling.
[04:41] Maya: That would help a lot. If Jonah can add a metric with team_tag, we can backfill for last quarter and show a real example.
[04:52] Jonah: I'll schedule the metric job and share a sample CSV.
[05:00] [00:05:20] Priya: Back to SOC 2: auditors will want to see evidence for user provisioning and SSO/SAML flows plus RBAC proofs. We should ensure our SSO audit logs are preserved for 12 months.
[05:20] Diego: We rotate SSO log retention between 6 and 18 months depending on environment; for prod it's 18 months. I'll confirm retention windows and add to the scoping doc.
[05:35] Priya: Also need to map who has admin roles in the console and get attestations.
[05:42] Samira: Ok — Priya to tag evidence owners, Diego to confirm retention.
[05:48] Oliver: Small note on treasury: if we move more teams to reserved commitments, we may want a centralized purchase to gain volume discounts. That will require a finance approval workflow change.
[06:00] Ethan: We can model that in the scenarios — centralized purchase with internal allocation versus decentralized purchases.
[06:08] Samira: Great. Now, runbook updates — last incident we had confusion on the escalation path. The on-call rotation page is out-of-date.
[06:19] Jonah: I noticed that — the rota still lists Kelsey who left in Nov. I'll update the on-call and the paging matrix; also add a quick checklist for investigating cost spikes (routing rules, debug snapshots, CI headers).
[06:33] Samira: Let's capture a short post-mortem template too so Finance can take the items they need for billing reconciliation.
[06:40] Maya: I'll take that.
[06:45] [00:07:10] Hannah: A question — Diego, is there any downtime expected during the KMS rotation? We need to schedule outside business hours if there's a maintenance window.
[07:00] Diego: Rotation for customer-managed keys typically is rolling and should be transparent. HSM-backed rotations might require brief rekeys; I'd estimate a 2–5 minute rekey window per region if we do it carefully. We can stage across regions.
[07:18] Priya: Auditors love to see no-downtime rotations; if we can document the rolling approach with test runs, that's ideal.
[07:27] Diego: I'll schedule a dry-run in staging and note the exact windows.
[07:33] Samira: Jonah, can you run a small bench that simulates the previous holiday embeddings job but constrained to a dev account so we can show cost per token and KV cache behavior?
[07:45] Jonah: Yes, I'll create a sample workload and run the bench. I think a 30-min run should be enough to capture token-level metrics.
[07:52] Ethan: If we can get that data next Tuesday, Finance can plug it into the chargeback model.
[08:00] Jonah: Targeting Monday night to run and have CSV by Tuesday morning.
[08:06] [00:09:05] Samira: Any blockers on the SOC 2 evidence collection? Priya?
[09:12] Priya: Main blocker is identifying evidence owners for older services. We lost some documentation during platform changeover. I'm asking service owners to nominate evidence reps.
[09:24] Maya: We also need a retention policy for debug snapshots and console logs — Finance is concerned about PII risk in unexpected debug outputs.
[09:36] Diego: Agree — I'll add scrub rules to the snapshot toolchain and prevent snapshots containing certain fields from being persisted. We might need a small regex-based scrubber.
[09:50] Priya: Please ensure scrubber's false positives are low; auditors want to see traceability.
[09:57] Diego: We'll log scrub actions and preserve hashes for traceability.
[10:05] [00:11:20] Hannah: For the chargeback model, can we also include a cap-ex amortization schedule for Reserved commits in the hybrid scenario? That will make finance forecasting accurate.
[10:35] Ethan: Good idea, amortize over 12 months with utilization adjusters.
[10:40] Samira: Noted — Hannah & Ethan to collaborate.
[10:44] [00:12:05] Maya: Small ops note — we should add a "billing incident" tag to the incident templates so that we can quickly flag and pull metrics for billing reconciliation.
[12:10] Jonah: I'll add that tag in PagerDuty + Opsgenie rules and make sure it propagates to the metrics pipeline.
[12:18] Samira: Excellent. Any other items?
[12:24] Oliver: One more from Treasury: if we centralize purchases we'll need an approval workflow with a two-step signoff for >$50k commitments.
[12:36] Ethan: We'll include that in the scenarios as a governance lever.
[12:42] [00:13:05] Samira: Alright let's recap. Action summary: Jonah patch header guard + metric tag + bench run; Diego KMS rotation plan + scrubber and retention windows; Priya finalize SOC 2 scoping & evidence owner list; Hannah build chargeback model scenarios; Maya and Ethan help with job list and forecast numbers; Samira will circulate runbook updates and the post-mortem template.
[13:20] Priya: One scheduling note — auditors requested a follow-up tech walkthrough week of Feb 2. Can we tentatively block 60 minutes?
[13:34] Samira: I'll send a calendar invite and include SEs.
[13:40] [00:14:00] Hannah: I'll aim to have initial chargeback slides by Jan 28 for the ops review.
[14:05] Jonah: And CSV metrics by Jan 19.
[14:12] Samira: Great. If no other items we'll wrap. Thanks everyone.
[14:20] [00:14:50] End of meeting.
